subject: Care plan structure & discount counteroffer
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Barnes <kelly.barnes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Care plan options and preliminary pricing

Hi Kelly —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call, I attached a short one-pager (care_plan_v1.pdf) that lays out three support/care tiers we commonly offer to customers running production inference with strict latency and availability targets. High level:

- Standard Care: 9x5 email support, best-effort response within 24 business hours, access to knowledge base and monthly review.
- Business Care: 12x5 phone+email, 8-hour response for Sev 1, named technical contact, quarterly health reviews.
- Enterprise Care: 24x7 on-call coverage, 2-hour initial response for Sev 1, weekly rollout coordination and prioritized engineering triage.

Pricing (indicative, USD/month):
- Standard: $2,500
- Business: $7,500
- Enterprise: $25,000

We typically offer an annual prepay discount (10%) and can quote committed throughput bands to lock in pricing. For Enterprise customers who want 24/7 escalation coverage and a dedicated on-call rotation, we add an operations retainer; I called that out in the attachment.

Questions for you: what uptime target and average QPS does Acme expect to run in production? If you can share an expected monthly token/embedding volume or sustained RPS, I can produce an options table that maps capacity tiers to price and an explicit discount for a 12–24 month commit.

If it helps I can also put together a short SOW for the Enterprise package (escalation flows, on-call SLAs, credit policy). Next week calendar is fairly open — tell me a couple of times that work and I’ll set up a follow-up with product ops.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: care_plan_v1.pdf (1 page — tier summary, discount grid)

From: Kelly Barnes <kelly.barnes@acmecorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Care plan options and preliminary pricing

Camila —

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications:

- Our target availability is 99.99% for inference endpoints (we run mission-critical scoring across sales and fraud).
- Expected baseline is ~250 RPS with a burst profile up to ~1,200 RPS for peak windows.
- We will require 24x7 escalation for Sev 1 incidents with a guaranteed engagement from an on-call engineer; 2-hour initial response is acceptable, but we may ask for faster for P1.

On pricing: the Enterprise list price is above our current budget for a single location. If Acme commits to a 12‑month contract and pays annually up front, we would expect a deeper discount — target is in the 20–25% range.

Also, procurement needs to see the credit policy (how uptime shortfalls translate to credits) and an outline of escalation responsibilities (who performs on-call, what’s included vs professional services). Can you share a sample SOW and any standard contract redlines?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call next Tue or Wed afternoon PT.
Kelly
Kelly Barnes
VP, Infrastructure — Acme Corp
procurement@acmecorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0110

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme asks on discount depth + escalation model

Aditya/Marissa —

Looping you in on Acme. They want Enterprise-level 24x7 escalation, target availability 99.99%, baseline ~250 RPS with peaks to ~1,200 RPS. Procurement is pushing for 20–25% off Enterprise list price with a 12-month annual prepay. They also want the credit policy and standard SOW/redlines.

Thoughts / authority: what discount can I offer without SE/RevOps approval? Is there a standard credit table we can share, or do we need to craft a special uptime-credit schedule for this account? Also, do we have a documented on-call escalation package that defines response windows and engineering engagement (pager model vs. prioritized support queue)?

I can propose a counter that includes a deeper commit term (24 months) in return for a larger discount and an ops retainer for guaranteed on-call rotation. Want to confirm acceptable concessions before I reply.

Thanks — Camila

[Internal note: this message is internal to Redwood. Do not forward to customer.]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Barnes <kelly.barnes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Care plan options and preliminary pricing

Kelly —

Thanks for the clarity and the availability windows. We discussed internally and can make the following counterproposal to balance Acme's budget and your uptime/escalation requirements:

Proposal (Enterprise Care — tuned for Acme):
- Availability banding: 99.995% (target), 99.95% (guaranteed). For availability measured below 99.95% in any quarterly period, Acme would receive a credit equal to 4 weeks of the monthly Enterprise retainer for that quarter.
- Response times: 24x7 on-call with 2-hour initial engagement for Sev 1; P1 escalations escalate to engineering triage with 4-hour SLA for action plan and 12-hour SLA for mitigation steps. We can include an option for 60-minute initial engagement for truly critical endpoints as an add-on.
- Pricing: Enterprise list $25,000/month. Counteroffer options: 15% discount for a 12-month prepaid commitment (net $21,250/mo equivalent), or 20% discount for a 24-month prepaid commitment (net $20,000/mo equivalent).
- Operations retainer: included in the Enterprise package (covers prioritized triage, weekend pager rotation for critical incidents). Any dedicated professional services (on-site runbooks, migration engineering) billed separately per SOW.

We will provide a short SOW and an example credit policy doc. I’ve attached our escalation flow diagram in redwood_escalation_oncall.pdf and added links below to the HubSpot deal and a draft SOW in Drive. If the 20% target is firm from Acme, we can explore a structured alternative: 12-month commitment at 15% + $40k one-time onboarding/ops retainer to bridge the gap.

Next steps: pick one of the pricing options (15% / 20% / 15%+retainer) and confirm whether you want the 60-minute P1 add-on. Once you confirm, I’ll send a draft SOW and a DocuSign-ready amendment for the committed term.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
